# MaineHealth Lincoln Hospital Celebrates Opening of New Infusion Center and Oncology & Blood Disorder Practice

August 31, 2026

DAMARISCOTTA, Maine – MaineHealth Lincoln Hospital celebrated the opening of its new Infusion Center and Oncology & Blood Disorder Practice on Aug. 31 with a ribbon-cutting ceremony attended by hospital leaders, care team members, board members, elected officials and community partners.

The new center brings infusion services together with oncology and blood disorder care in o

Image: MaineHealth Lincoln Hospital clinicians and leaders stand together in a group behind a large red ribbon

Photo caption (left to right): Lincoln Wellness Rehab Manager Kelly Creamer; MaineHealth Lincoln Hospital President Cindy Wade; Regional Representative for U.S. Senator Angus S. King, Jr. Scott Wilkinson; Associate Medical Director, MaineHealth Cancer Care Damariscotta Hillary Glick, MD; MaineHealth Lincoln Hospital Manager of Infusion Service Melissa Brown; State Office Representative for U.S. Senator Susan Collins Chuck Mahaleris; Coastal Region Nursing Officer Christine Anderson, RN; Lincoln Wellness Supervisor Laura Smith

ne centralized location, expanding access to specialized treatment and improving convenience for patients receiving care close to home. 

Located on the third floor of MaineHealth Lincoln Hospital in the renovated Wellness and Therapy space, the new center was designed to meet growing demand for oncology and infusion services in Lincoln County while making care easier to access and navigate for patients and families. The facility offers chemotherapy, immunotherapy, IV infusions, medication injections, blood product transfusions, therapeutic phlebotomy, central line care, oncology and hematology appointments, chemotherapy education and social work support.

The project also increases infusion treatment capacity, helping more patients receive timely appointments locally while strengthening coordination between oncology providers and infusion care teams. Patients can register directly within the department, reducing unnecessary stops and streamlining their care experience. 

By increasing infusion treatment chairs from five to nine, the new center will help more patients receive the care they need sooner and closer to home. With more than 600 infusion patients served last year, the expanded space is expected to increase treatment capacity by 40 percent.

The new center reflects MaineHealth Lincoln Hospital's continued investment in services that meet community needs and expand access to specialized care close to home. The project was supported in part by a $4.5 million Congressional Directed Spending award led by Senators Susan Collins and Angus King to expand oncology and infusion services in Damariscotta.

“This new center reflects years of planning, investment and collaboration on behalf of our community,” said Cindy Wade, RN, BSN, MHA, President of MaineHealth Lincoln Hospital. “We are grateful for the support of our US Senators, donors, care team members and community partners who helped make this project possible. Most importantly, this investment strengthens access to care for people throughout Lincoln County by allowing more patients to receive oncology and infusion treatments close to home, reducing travel burdens and making care easier to access and navigate for patients and families.”

“Bringing oncology and infusion services together in one space allows us to provide more coordinated care and better support patients throughout their treatment journey,” said Melissa Brown, MaineHealth Lincoln Hospital Manager of Infusion Services. “The new center improves efficiency for patients and care teams, expands our capacity to serve more people locally and helps ensure patients can access the specialized services they need.” 

Hospital leaders recognized the many individuals and teams whose work helped bring the project to completion, including members of the infusion and oncology care teams, hospital operations and leadership teams, and partners involved in the design and construction of the new center.

# Port City Veterinary Referral Hospital Expands as Comprehensive Cancer Center with Launch of Radiation Oncology Services

Image: Cover Image for Port City Veterinary Referral Hospital Expands as Comprehensive Cancer Center with Launch of Radiation Oncology Services 

The First and Only Facility in New Hampshire and Maine  

PORTSMOUTH, NH, UNITED STATES, October 8, 2025 -- FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE 
 
Port City Veterinary Referral Hospital, part of Ethos Veterinary Health, is proud to announce the launch of the Radiation Oncology services, led by board-certified radiation oncologist Dr. Maegan Watson-Skaggs, DVM, DACVR-RO (Radiation Oncology). With this addition, Port City becomes the only veterinary radiation oncology facility in New Hampshire and Maine, extending access to advanced oncology care for pets across New England and into Canada. 
 
🔸A Comprehensive Cancer Center for Pets🔸 
 
Port City’s expansion marks its expansion into a Comprehensive Cancer Center, offering both Radiation Oncology and Medical Oncology under one roof.  

Dr. Megan Duckett, DVM, DACVIM (Medical Oncology) 
Working alongside Dr. Watson, Dr. Duckett provides comprehensive Medical Oncology services, including chemotherapy, targeted therapies, and personalized treatment planning. Her approach centers on compassionate, evidence-based care and collaboration with pet families and primary veterinarians. By combining her expertise with advanced diagnostics and therapeutic options, Dr. Duckett helps ensure each patient receives the most effective and humane path forward. 
 
Together, Dr. Watson and Dr. Duckett lead a unified oncology program, giving pets access to the full spectrum of cancer treatment options in one location. 
 
➤Expanding Access to Oncology in New England 
Pet owners across New Hampshire, Maine, Vermont, Massachusetts, and beyond now have local on-site access to both Radiation and Medical Oncology without the need for extensive travel. This milestone reinforces Port City’s mission to combine innovation, collaboration, and compassion in the fight against cancer and complex diseases.
